main_text.p: Vehementia caloris à mediocritate recedens est in essentia, vel tenuiore vel crassiore.
In essentia tenuiore vehemens calor si fuerit, Acrimonia gignitur.
Acrimo-nia.Acrimonia est sapor vehementis calo-ris linguam mordicans, erodens, penetrans, & valdè dissolvens exsiccando, qualis est in Pipere, Zinzibere, Allio, Cœ-pis, &c.

p.i: Hinc Medici Physici docent acria attenu-are & incidere: incidendo separare serosum humorem à sanguine, digerere halitus, & lapides ex materia pituitosa compactos disjicere.

main_text.p: In essentia crassiore est Salsedo & Amaritudo.
Salsedo.Salsedo est sapor abundantis caloris congregando & desiccando linguam detergens & abluens, ac gustui gratiam præbens, qualis est in Sale & paucis Plantis, quæ locis proveniunt salsis.

p.i: Hic igitur sapor, abstergendi, abluendi, exsiccandi, & putrefactionem prohibendi facultate pollet. Hinc falsa dicuntur exsiccare, & absumere humiditates. Hinc est, quod mollem indurant carnem, & duram reddunt molliorem. In illa enim absumunt superfluam hu-

page.notes: The curved pen strokes over "essentia", "Acrimonia" and "Pipere" are handwritten annotations and were left out. The catchword "midita-" sits below the rule at the foot of the page and continues the last line. The long s has been rendered as a plain s throughout. The printed word in the Salsedo paragraph may be "desiccando" (the letter shape is somewhat unclear).
